source_title: Assessing the environmental footprint of alternative green biorefinery protein extraction techniques from grasses and legumes
authors: James Gaffey; Andres Arce Matinez; Thalles Allan Andrade; Morten Ambye-Jensen; George Bishop; Maurice N. Collins; David Styles
source_type: Peer-reviewed open-access article; Table 3 LCI reference
material: Irish/Danish cultivated perennial ryegrass and grass-clover; one-stage and multi-stage green biorefinery; brown-juice AD LCI scenarios
quality_notes: 42 Table 3 flow records per 1 t DM LPC-CP reference flow. Demonstration-plant mass/energy and product yields are primary campaign data scaled to FU; agriculture, AD, nutrient credits and emissions are modelled LCI. Negative coproduct entries are credits, not physical negative flows. Heat input unit kW has unclear time basis. Supplementary workbook is listed but its download endpoint returned 403; only manuscript Table 3 is transcribed. CC BY 4.0 article license noted by institutional repository.

source_title: GHG Emission Factors for Electricity Consumption
authors: Joana Bastos; Fabio Monforti-Ferrario; Giulia Melica
material: Netherlands national electricity-consumption life-cycle factor; Table3_EU_LC!AH21; 2021 observation
quality_notes: Official JRC dataset, CC BY 4.0, publicly downloadable without authentication. Raw workbook cell AH21 is 0.406463499759293 t CO2e/MWh; model screening value is 0.406463 kg CO2e/kWh. Includes upstream supply-chain emissions; national consumption mix, not supplier-specific; temporal coverage through 2021. Screening-only, not activated by default.

source_title: Chain emissions for heat grids in 2022 and 2030
quality_notes: CE Delft publication page reports total 2022 end-user heat factor 30.96 kg CO2e/GJ, comprising direct and supply-chain emissions; model converts by 277.7778 kWh/GJ to 0.111456 kg CO2e/kWh. No DOI found; stable local source ID is used.

source_title: Life Cycle Assessment of roadside grass verges in Flanders
authors: Rahul Ravi (editor); Marcella Fernandes De Souza (contributor)
material: Consequential cradle-to-farm-gate comparison of windrow composting against roadside-grass/pig-manure co-digestion; 1 t mowed grass functional unit
quality_notes: Public project report, 12 pages; scenario impact results and boundary recorded separately. The report states full LCI is available on GitHub on request. No DOI or explicit reuse license identified. Results include avoided energy, fertilizer and biowaste-treatment burdens; never interpret them as gross emissions or GreenHub-specific factors.

source_title: Environmental impacts of a biorefinery integrated into dairy farming system
authors: Narta Elshani; Steffen Adler; Pernilla Tidåker; Jon Kristian Sommerseth; Matthias Koesling; Håvard Steinshamn
material: Tuv NIBIO pilot green biorefinery; grass-clover forage; aggregate measured facility energy per Mg dry matter
quality_notes: Primary study reports 375 kWh electricity and 138 MJ propane heat per Mg DM biomass; electricity was measured at unit operations and published as a whole-facility total in the article. Norwegian grass-clover system; report-only cross-study benchmark, not a route-specific GreenHub factor.

source_title: Methane loss from commercially operating biogas upgrading plants
material: Nine commercial Danish upgrader samples: three amine, four water scrubber and two membrane; gas quality before/after upgrading and off-gas; methane loss relative to supplied methane
quality_notes: Plant table reproduced in IEA Bioenergy Task 37 (2025), Table 6, pp. 13–14, and attributed there to this article. Primary abstract reports mean methane loss 0.81% of supplied methane, technology extremes 0.04–1.97%, and 99.5% reduction of methane in a selected waste gas using RTO. Gas quality basis, scale, feedstocks, sampling replication and plant identities are not reported in the reproduced table. No reuse license identified; reference-only and not a GreenHub default. Retrieved 2026-11-07.

source_title: Methane losses from different biogas plant technologies
authors: Viktoria Wechselberger; Torsten Reinelt; Johan Yngvesson; Deborah Scharfy; Charlotte Scheutz; Marion Huber-Humer; Marlies Hrad
source_type: peer-reviewed measurement article with open Zenodo raw data, glossary and analysis code
material: Harmonized methane-emission measurements from AD digesters, digestate storage, CHP units, gas upgrading units and equipment rooms at 33 plants in Austria, Germany, Sweden and Switzerland
quality_notes: Table 2 aggregate extract and verbatim Zenodo v2 source files (294 records, 32 fields, glossary and R Markdown code) are retained. The Zenodo v1 record displays CC BY 4.0; v2 states its data are the same as v1 but omits a separate rights statement. Mixed substrates and technology contexts; reference-only, not GreenHub defaults or grass-specific factors.
